title: A Multi-Dimensional, Per-Pass Empirical Study of the LLVM Optimization Pipeline
abstract: arXiv:2606.31238v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Quantifying the marginal impact of individual optimization passes underpins phase ordering, pass selection, optimization design, and analysis of pass/hardware interactions. In LLVM, the standard backend for C/C++, Rust, and ML stacks via MLIR, interactions among passes, measurement noise, and pipeline scale make this difficult. We present a systematic empirical study of the LLVM -O3 pipeline. We decompose it into 113 cumulative per-pass prefixes and measure execution time, compile time, binary size, hardware counters, and RAPL energy on 30 PolyBench/C kernels (84,750 measurements). Transitions whose binary is byte-identical to their predecessor give us a built-in null distribution, which we use to calibrate every significance claim. On these compute-bound affine kernels, the pipeline is non-monotone: 36% of the transitions that significantly change runtime are regressions, found in 28 of 30 kernels. tldr: 通过将LLVM的-O3优化流水线分解为113个累积遍前缀、在30个PolyBench/C内核上进行84,750次多维测量，该研究利用字节级相同的二进制构建零分布来校准显著性，首次系统揭示了该流水线是非单调的——36%显著改变运行时间的优化遍转换实际上是性能回退。
en_tdlr: By decomposing LLVM's -O3 pipeline into 113 cumulative per-pass prefixes and performing 84,750 multi-dimensional measurements on 30 PolyBench/C kernels, this study uses byte-identical binaries as a built-in null distribution to calibrate significance, systematically revealing for the first time that the pipeline is non-monotone, with 36% of significant runtime-changing transitions being regressions.
